title: Getting a consistent hand-painted storybook look from AI images: the pipeline behind my Ghost Month horror game
author: Last-Ad-6081
selftext:
I'm making Tending Grave, a narrative horror game set in a Vietnamese village cemetery during Ghost Month. Everything visual started from FLUX via fal.ai. Here's what kept it looking like one book instead of fifty prompts:

\- \*\*One style, locked.\*\* A single moodboard painting is the style reference, and every prompt starts with the same style prefix. Scenes with characters pass the character sheets as references.

\- \*\*One painting per area.\*\* Each area is one continuous background (ground, graves, trees in mist), generated with the previous area as the reference. A Python script cuts out the sky, moves the ground line to the same pixel row on every page and matches the soil colour row by row, so pages line up. Seams hide behind a foreground banyan tree.

\- \*\*Paper puppets, not sprites.\*\* The model paints a sheet of body parts; a script splits them by alpha; joints are measured on the image and Unity animates the rig (walk, idle, reach, startle). The first torso had the near arm painted on and a playtester said the character looked paralysed, so the arm was erased offline and is now its own part.

\- \*\*Things the model gets wrong unless you say it.\*\* Vietnamese graves have curved tiled roofs and incense bowls, not crosses. No text in images at all (the UI draws every word). Side-view vehicles drift onto roads that recede into the distance.

\- \*\*Fix offline instead of re-rolling.\*\* Background removal deleted grey tombstones on white, so it's a flood fill now. The moss on gravestones is composited from the clean painting, so the scrubbing mini-game reveals exactly the clean stone underneath.

\- \*\*Audio:\*\* sound effects and ambience from ElevenLabs, music from Stable Audio. The loops weren't seamless, so every loop crossfades with itself.

Still weak: side characters are single images, and keeping a character consistent across many poses is hard.

Free demo (Chapter 1, about an hour, browser and mobile): [https://vgamclub.itch.io/tending-grave](https://vgamclub.itch.io/tending-grave)
